places.name: Neue Nationalgalerie
places.note: Mies's steel and glass temple of 1968, carefully restored by Chipperfield. The empty upper hall is the exhibit.

places.name: Philharmonie
places.note: Scharoun's tent of gold, the orchestra in the middle and terraces of seats around it. Book a lunchtime concert or a tour.

places.name: Neues Museum
places.note: Chipperfield's repair of a bombed museum, scars kept, new brick stitched into old. Nefertiti waits under her own dome.

places.name: Jewish Museum Berlin
places.note: Libeskind's zinc-clad zigzag, cut through with voids you look into but cannot enter. Architecture that makes absence physical.

places.name: Sammlung Boros
places.note: A wartime bunker holding a private collection of contemporary art; the owners live on top. Guided tours only, in small groups; book weeks ahead.

places.name: Hamburger Bahnhof
places.note: A 19th-century railway terminus for contemporary art, with the long shed behind it for the big installations.

places.name: Kaiser Wilhelm Memorial Church
places.note: Eiermann's 1961 octagon of blue glass blocks beside the bombed spire. Step inside and the light turns everything cobalt.

places.name: Tempelhofer Feld
places.note: A closed airport given back to the city as open field. Runways for cycling and kites, and the biggest sky in Berlin.

places.name: Hufeisensiedlung
places.note: Bruno Taut's horseshoe estate of the 1920s, coloured doors, gardens and all. Modernist housing that is still loved.

places.name: Do You Read Me?!
places.note: A small shop for independent magazines on art, design and fashion. Leave with more than you meant to.
